recurring_scale_anchors: 304×192 canvas; keep symptoms and first-aid cues readable but mild, non-graphic and suitable for general vocabulary learning.
No readable words, labels, numbers or brands; use clear silhouettes, body-location highlights and simple medical objects only.

Use the chapter group to resolve ambiguous terms: rash is a skin eruption, burn is a skin injury, cut is a wound, cold is the common illness, temperature is body temperature, and ER is the emergency room.
Differentiate overlapping symptoms through body location, posture and one specific medical cue; do not use a thermometer as the only cue for every illness.
Avoid blood, bodily fluids and severe injury details; imply care with a bandage, ice pack, inhaler, tissue or clinic when relevant.

polysemy_resolution_table.ache: A continuous dull physical pain, shown by a person rubbing a sore body area; broader and more persistent than one sharp pain.
polysemy_resolution_table.backache: Dull pain in the lower back, clearly located along the lumbar area.
polysemy_resolution_table.cough: A forceful expulsion from the throat or lungs, shown as coughing into a bent elbow or tissue.
polysemy_resolution_table.fever: An abnormally high body temperature, shown by a flushed, chilled person and thermometer.
polysemy_resolution_table.headache: Pain in the head, shown by pressing the temples; keep the cue mild and distinct from migraine.
polysemy_resolution_table.hurt: To cause physical pain or injury to someone, shown by a person reacting to a gentle accidental bump.
polysemy_resolution_table.ill: Generally unwell with a need to rest or receive care; not specifically nausea.
polysemy_resolution_table.itchy: A prickly skin sensation that makes a person scratch a small area.
polysemy_resolution_table.migraine: A severe headache with strong light sensitivity, represented by a darkened room and one-sided head pain.
polysemy_resolution_table.pain: A physical unpleasant sensation localized in a body area, broader and less specifically dull than ache.
polysemy_resolution_table.painful: An action or body area that hurts when touched or moved, shown through a guarded movement.
polysemy_resolution_table.runny nose: A congested nose with clear nasal discharge and tissues; keep it separate from a sneeze in progress.
polysemy_resolution_table.sick: Unwell with nausea or stomach discomfort in this illness context; distinguish from broadly ill.
polysemy_resolution_table.sneeze: A sudden burst of air from nose and mouth, with a tissue covering both.
polysemy_resolution_table.sore: A body part tender and painful when touched, shown as a localized sensitive spot without an open wound.
polysemy_resolution_table.sore throat: A painful, irritated throat, shown by a person gently holding their throat and a simple throat illustration.
polysemy_resolution_table.stomachache / stomach ache: Pain in the abdomen, with a hand pressing the belly; distinguish from lower-right appendicitis.
polysemy_resolution_table.swollen: A body part enlarged by inflammation, such as a puffed ankle; no broken bone is implied.
polysemy_resolution_table.symptom / symptoms: Observable signs of illness, shown by a small set of distinct cues such as cough, fever and rash.
polysemy_resolution_table.temperature: A person’s body temperature measured with a clinical thermometer; not outdoor air or weather temperature.
polysemy_resolution_table.vomit: To bring stomach contents up; imply nausea and a nearby basin without graphic contents.
polysemy_resolution_table.rash: A patch of irritated spots on skin, using the sickness noun sense; not the adjective meaning reckless.
polysemy_resolution_table.accident: An unintended mishap that causes a mild injury, shown by a stumble or dropped object; not chance in the abstract.
polysemy_resolution_table.bite: A small animal bite wound or tooth mark in the injury context; not taking a bite from food.
polysemy_resolution_table.bleed: Blood coming from a small wound; use a minimal red mark or bandage, never graphic detail.
polysemy_resolution_table.broken bone: A fracture represented through a simple X-ray or a supported cast; not a visible bone.
polysemy_resolution_table.bruise: A purple discoloration under intact skin after a bump.
polysemy_resolution_table.burn: A mild heat injury to skin with a small red tender patch; not a flame or fuel burning.
polysemy_resolution_table.cut (wound): A small superficial opening in skin made by a sharp edge; not food preparation.
polysemy_resolution_table.injury: Physical harm from an accident, represented by a guarded limb or a bandage; broader than a bruise or cut.
polysemy_resolution_table.nosebleed: A small amount of blood from the nose, with tissue held under the nostrils; keep it mild.
polysemy_resolution_table.splinter: A tiny sliver of wood embedded in a fingertip and removed with tweezers.
polysemy_resolution_table.sprain: A twisted ligament around an ankle or wrist, shown with gentle swelling and a support wrap; not a fracture.
polysemy_resolution_table.sting: A small insect puncture and the painful reaction, such as the bee stinging a fingertip; not an animal bite.
polysemy_resolution_table.allergies: An immune reaction such as itchy eyes and skin after exposure to common triggers; broader than pollen hay fever.
polysemy_resolution_table.appendicitis: Inflammation in the lower-right abdomen, represented by a simple body-location diagram and medical care.
polysemy_resolution_table.asthma: Breathing difficulty eased by an inhaler, without distress or emergency framing.
polysemy_resolution_table.chickenpox: A child with a mild, widespread itchy spotted rash; distinguish from a small localized rash.
polysemy_resolution_table.cold (sickness): The common cold with congestion, tissues and mild fatigue; not cold weather or chills alone.
polysemy_resolution_table.diabetes: A person checks blood glucose with a meter or uses routine insulin care; no diagnosis text or numbers.
polysemy_resolution_table.diarrhea: Digestive illness causing urgent bathroom use and stomach cramping; imply the symptom without bodily fluids.
polysemy_resolution_table.eczema: A dry, irritated skin patch, shown as a localized recurring condition; not an infectious rash.
polysemy_resolution_table.flu: A strong viral illness with bed rest, fever and body aches; distinguish from a mild common cold.
polysemy_resolution_table.food poisoning: Sudden stomach illness after eating contaminated food; use a questionable meal and nausea cue, no graphic vomiting.
polysemy_resolution_table.hay fever: Pollen allergy with watery eyes and sneezing outdoors near flowering plants; more specific than general allergies.
polysemy_resolution_table.high blood pressure: Elevated blood pressure being checked with a cuff and gauge; no numbers or labels.
polysemy_resolution_table.indigestion: Upper-abdominal discomfort after a meal, shown by a full plate and a person rubbing the upper stomach.
polysemy_resolution_table.infection: Germs entering a small wound or causing localized inflammation; use a simple magnified germ cue.
polysemy_resolution_table.insomnia: Difficulty sleeping at night, shown by an awake person in bed under moonlight.
polysemy_resolution_table.measles: A widespread spotted viral rash with a mildly unwell child; not a few chickenpox-like blisters.
polysemy_resolution_table.mumps: Swelling around the cheeks and jaw, with a mild sore face cue.
polysemy_resolution_table.stress: Emotional or mental strain shown by a tense posture and crowded everyday demands; not physical pressure.
polysemy_resolution_table.tonsillitis: Inflamed tonsils visible as red spots at the back of a simple mouth/throat diagram.
polysemy_resolution_table.virus: A generic microscopic virus particle with a spiky envelope under magnification; not a named disease.
polysemy_resolution_table.doctor: A medical professional examining and helping a patient; keep the existing stethoscope-and-patient illustration if clear.
polysemy_resolution_table.ER: Emergency room / emergency department care, shown by an urgent hospital entrance and ambulance; not the chemical element erbium.
polysemy_resolution_table.urgent care: A walk-in clinic for prompt but non-emergency treatment; distinguish from an ambulance-led emergency room.

glossary_context_notes: The lesson groups resolve rash as a skin symptom, burn and cut as injuries, cold as the common illness, body temperature as a clinical measurement and ER as emergency room.
Separate ache, pain, painful, sore and hurt through duration, location and action; separate a bite from a sting, and a sprain from a broken bone.
Keep clinical cues low detail and non-graphic; avoid readable text and numerical readings.

It shows a person coughing into the bent elbow, the correct respiratory-health cue for this lesson.
The tissue covers the nose and mouth while sudden motion marks show a sneeze, distinct from the cough candidate.
A hand gently protects one tender shoulder spot; it shows soreness without an open cut.
The thermometer is outdoors with sun and landscape cues, so it teaches ambient weather temperature, not body temperature.
It shows a hand taking a bite from an apple; this is food eating, not an injury bite.
A clear purple mark lies beneath intact skin, which directly teaches a bruise.
A flame burns in a pan, not a skin injury.
A small red tender patch on intact skin with a cool compress clearly shows a mild burn injury.
It shows a narrow superficial skin cut and a nearby bandage without a food-preparation scene.
A knife cuts a tomato on a board, which is food preparation rather than a wound.
A bee’s stinger contacts a fingertip, directly teaching an insect sting.
The person is shivering in snowy weather, teaching low temperature rather than the common cold.
A doctor with a stethoscope examines a patient, a clear medical-care scene.
It shows a household pan fire and responders, teaching a general emergency rather than the hospital emergency room.
